children.name: Cached Forager v3
children.hypothesis: The previous mandatory deposit rules cause agents to carry empty loads or rest prematurely due to rigid synchronization; adding a 'carrying' condition specifically to trigger 'deposit' only when cargo is full prevents unnecessary stops at non-full locations, allowing faster travel between food patches while still ensuring all harvested items are stored upon arrival.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Strategic Storage
children.hypothesis: Previous attempts failed because mandatory deposit rules forced agents to stop at non-full locations (causing zero harvests) or triggered premature resting due to rigid timing. The new policy combines the successful 'always deposit' momentum of child-0024 with an energy-based threshold for gathering, allowing full loads to be carried without stopping unless energy is critically low (<28), which prevents depletion while maximizing trips per 720 steps.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Threshold Heuristics
children.hypothesis: Previous mandatory deposit and rigid rest rules caused agents to stop prematurely or fail to harvest due to poor synchronization with food patch locations; this hypothesis posits that relaxing the deposit condition to only trigger when cargo exceeds capacity by 1 unit, combined with a dynamic rest interval based on remaining steps rather than fixed ticks, will maximize trips per 720 steps while preventing energy depletion.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Stacked Harvest
children.hypothesis: The previous 'carrying' deposit rule caused agents to stop immediately after gathering one item, preventing full capacity utilization and increasing travel costs. By delaying the mandatory deposit until cargo reaches exactly 3 units (capacity), agents will carry multiple harvests per trip, significantly reducing total movement distance and maximizing food accumulation within 720 steps.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Efficient Rest-Deposit
children.hypothesis: Previous attempts failed because mandatory deposit rules caused agents to stop immediately after gathering one item, preventing full capacity utilization (cargo=1 instead of 3). By changing the 'carrying' condition to only trigger when cargo exceeds half capacity (cargo>1), agents will carry multiple harvests per trip. Combined with a fixed rest interval, this should maximize trips per 720 steps and stored food.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Batch Foraging
children.hypothesis: Previous attempts failed because agents deposited food immediately after gathering a single item (cargo=1), failing to utilize their capacity of 3. This led to excessive travel distance and energy expenditure, resulting in zero stored food for the agent population. By restricting the mandatory 'deposit' action to only trigger when the cargo count reaches exactly 2 (allowing one final item before full capacity is hit, ensuring a load of 3 upon departure), agents will maximize harvests per trip. Combined with the existing energy-based rest logic, this strategy optimizes movement efficiency and stored food accumulation.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Full-Load Optimization
children.hypothesis: Previous attempts failed because mandatory deposit rules triggered immediately after gathering a single item (cargo=1), preventing full capacity utilization (cargo=3) and causing agents to carry less than their maximum load. This led to excessive travel distance per trip relative to food gained, effectively nullifying the benefit of fixed rest intervals. By changing the 'carrying' condition from `cargo>0` to `cargo>=2`, agents will only deposit once they have harvested enough items to be nearly full (ensuring a departure with cargo=3 if possible, or at least 2), thereby maximizing food per movement cycle and increasing total stored food within 720 steps.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Energy-Limited Foraging
children.hypothesis: Previous strategies prioritized cargo volume over energy conservation, forcing agents to deplete their energy reserves to reach maximum capacity (3 units) before depositing. This high-energy cost per trip resulted in premature exhaustion and zero stored food. By switching the mandatory deposit trigger from a cargo-based condition ('carrying') to an energy-based condition ('tired'), agents will stop at the optimal point where they are most fatigued rather than full, balancing movement efficiency with survival. Combined with a fixed rest interval, this ensures agents return home frequently without over-extending their limited energy pool.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.hypothesis: Previous attempts failed because mandatory deposit rules triggered immediately after gathering a single item (cargo=1), preventing full capacity utilization and causing agents to carry less than their maximum load. By changing the 'carrying' condition from cargo>=0 to cargo>0 but delaying the first mandatory deposit until the agent has harvested enough items to be nearly full (specifically, requiring 2 items before the first forced deposit), agents will maximize food per movement cycle and increase total stored food within 720 steps.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Threshold Deposit Protocol
children.hypothesis: The repeated failure of mandatory deposit rules stems from agents forcing a return trip immediately after gathering only one item, leaving them under-capacity and unable to amortize travel costs. Evidence shows that maximizing cargo volume (aiming for 3 units) before depositing significantly improves food-per-distance ratios. The optimal strategy is to combine the energy-based trigger for resting (tired: rest) with a strict volume-based trigger for depositing, but specifically delayed until the agent has accumulated 2 items. This ensures agents gather two items then move to the nearest food source to harvest a third, creating a full load (cargo=3), before finally depositing. This maximizes the efficiency of each outbound journey.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Cache Optimization
children.hypothesis: Previous mandatory deposit strategies failed because forcing a return trip after only one item (cargo=1) or two items (cargo=2) resulted in suboptimal load factors and excessive travel distances per food unit harvested. The optimal approach is to delay mandatory deposition until the agent reaches full capacity (cargo=3), allowing them to gather three items before returning home. This maximizes the food-per-trip ratio, ensuring agents utilize their full energy reserves efficiently for maximum harvest volume rather than stopping prematurely due to artificial cargo thresholds.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Full-Load Protocol
children.hypothesis: Previous mandatory deposit rules failed because agents were forced to return after accumulating only 1 or 2 items, resulting in low cargo volumes and high travel-to-harvest ratios. The evidence shows that maximizing load before returning yields better energy efficiency. This rule changes the deposition trigger from any non-zero cargo to a strict minimum of 3 items (full capacity), ensuring agents harvest three units before moving home. This maximizes food per trip distance and optimizes energy usage for the 720-step horizon.

revision.reason: Previous policy retained: requires improvement in both groups and no holdout regression.

children.author: Mara / qwen3.5:4b
children.name: Mara's Full Load Cache
children.hypothesis: Previous mandatory deposit rules failed because agents were forced to return with minimal loads (1 or 2 items), wasting the capacity of their 3-item storage and incurring high travel costs relative to food gained. The evidence shows that delaying the 'carrying' deposit trigger until the agent reaches full capacity (cargo=3) maximizes food per trip distance. By only forcing a return when the cargo count equals the maximum capacity (3), agents will accumulate more food before paying the energy penalty of travel, resulting in a higher net stored food count within the 720-step horizon.
